name: Nigerian Tacos
description: A bold Nigerian fusion taco filled with juicy suya-spiced beef, crisp coleslaw, fresh tomatoes, and spicy pepper sauce in crunchy taco shells. Street food meets fine dining in every bite.
instructions: Slice the beef into thin strips and season generously with suya spice.
Grill or stir-fry the beef until well cooked and slightly charred.
Blend the tatashe with a little scotch bonnet and onion, then fry briefly to make a spicy pepper sauce.
Warm the taco shells in the oven for 2–3 minutes until crisp.
Fill each taco shell with coleslaw.
Top with the cooked suya beef and sliced fresh tomatoes.
Drizzle with the pepper sauce and serve immediately.
author: API Food Database

name: Yam Fries with Spicy Dip
description: Crispy golden yam fries seasoned with aromatic spices and served alongside a creamy spicy pepper dipping sauce. A stylish Nigerian twist on classic fries that is crunchy on the outside, fluffy on the inside, and absolutely addictive.
instructions: Peel the yam and cut it into thick fry-shaped strips.
Rinse and pat the yam dry with a clean towel.
Season lightly with salt and mixed spice.
Heat the vegetable oil and deep fry the yam until golden brown and crispy on the outside.
Drain on paper towels to remove excess oil.
Blend or finely mince the scotch bonnet and mix it thoroughly with the mayonnaise to make a spicy dipping sauce.
Adjust the dip with a pinch of salt if desired.
Serve the hot yam fries immediately with the spicy dip.
author: API Food Database

name: Plantain Chips
description: Thin, crispy, and perfectly salted Nigerian plantain chips made from thinly sliced unripe plantain and deep-fried until golden. A popular Nigerian snack that's perfect for parties, road trips, or everyday munching.
instructions: Peel the unripe plantains and slice them very thinly using a sharp knife or mandoline.
Sprinkle the slices with salt and cayenne pepper, then toss lightly.
Heat the vegetable oil over medium-high heat.
Fry the plantain slices in batches until they become golden and crispy.
Remove and drain on paper towels.
Allow to cool completely to become extra crunchy.
Store in an airtight container or serve immediately.
author: API Food Database

name: Nigerian Meat Pie
description: A beloved Nigerian baked pastry with a buttery, flaky crust filled with well-seasoned minced beef, diced carrots, potatoes, and onions. Crispy on the outside and rich, juicy, and savory on the inside, it's a favorite snack for parties, picnics, and everyday enjoyment.
instructions: Mix flour and butter until the mixture resembles breadcrumbs.
Gradually add cold water and knead into a smooth dough. Cover and chill for 20 minutes.
Cook the minced beef with diced onions, carrots, potatoes, seasoning, and a little water until the filling is thick. Allow to cool completely.
Roll out the dough and cut into medium circles.
Place a generous spoonful of filling in the center of each circle.
Fold over, seal the edges with a fork, and brush with beaten egg if desired.
Bake in a preheated oven at 180°C for 25–30 minutes or until golden brown.
Allow to cool slightly before serving.
author: API Food Database

name: Nigerian Fish Roll
description: A popular Nigerian fried pastry snack filled with seasoned canned fish, onions, and peppers. Crispy golden outside with a savory fish filling inside — a street food favourite enjoyed by all ages.
instructions: Mix flour with butter, baking powder, salt, and water to form a soft dough.
Mash sardines with diced onion, scotch bonnet, and seasoning.
Roll dough into thin rectangles.
Place fish filling on one end and roll tightly.
Seal the edges firmly.
Deep fry in hot oil until golden brown and crispy.
Drain on paper towels and serve warm.
author: API Food Database

name: Sausage Roll
description: A classic Nigerian party snack of seasoned sausage wrapped in a flaky buttery pastry and baked until golden. A staple at every Nigerian children's party and adult gathering alike.
instructions: Mix flour, butter, mixed spice, and a pinch of salt until crumbly.
Gradually add cold water and knead into a smooth dough.
Cover and rest the dough for 20 minutes.
Roll the dough into a thin rectangle and cut into strips.
Wrap each sausage tightly in pastry and seal the edges.
Arrange on a baking tray and brush with beaten egg.
Bake at 180°C for 20–25 minutes until golden brown.
Allow to cool slightly and serve warm.
author: API Food Database

name: Nigerian Oxtail Stew
description: A luxurious and deeply flavored Nigerian slow-cooked oxtail stew with rich tomato sauce, aromatic spices, and fall-off-the-bone tender meat. A premium dish that rewards patience with extraordinary flavor.
instructions: Wash and season the oxtail with salt, seasoning cubes, onion, garlic, ginger, and thyme.
Cook until tender, reserving the stock.
Blend tomatoes, tatashe, onion, and scotch bonnet until smooth.
Heat vegetable oil and fry the blended mixture for 20–25 minutes until reduced.
Add the cooked oxtail and reserved stock.
Simmer gently for 25–30 minutes until the stew thickens and the meat absorbs the flavors.
Adjust seasoning and serve hot with white rice, boiled yam, potatoes, or bread.
author: API Food Database

name: Catfish Stew
description: A bold and flavorful Nigerian tomato stew made with fresh catfish pieces simmered in a rich blended pepper and tomato sauce. The catfish absorbs all the spices beautifully for a deeply satisfying meal.
instructions: Clean and cut the catfish into serving pieces; season lightly with salt and seasoning.
Blend tomatoes, tatashe, scotch bonnet, and onion until smooth.
Heat vegetable oil and fry the blended mixture for about 20 minutes until the raw taste disappears.
Season the stew with seasoning cubes, thyme, curry, and salt to taste.
Gently add the catfish pieces without stirring vigorously to prevent breaking.
Cover and simmer for 12–15 minutes until the fish is fully cooked.
Serve hot with white rice, boiled yam, plantain, or bread.
author: API Food Database

name: Nigerian Corned Beef Stew
description: A quick and satisfying Nigerian stew made from canned corned beef cooked in a rich tomato and pepper sauce. Perfect for busy weeknights and delicious with rice, yam, bread, or boiled plantain.
instructions: Blend tomatoes, onion, and scotch bonnet until smooth.
Heat vegetable oil and fry the blended mixture for about 10–15 minutes until the sauce thickens.
Season with curry, thyme, seasoning cubes, and salt to taste.
Add the corned beef and gently break it into chunks while stirring.
Allow the stew to simmer for another 8–10 minutes.
Adjust consistency with a little water if necessary.
Serve hot with white rice, boiled yam, potatoes, bread, or plantain.
author: API Food Database

name: Peppered Mushroom
description: Juicy mushrooms tossed in a rich and spicy Nigerian pepper sauce. A delicious vegetarian dish with a satisfying meaty texture, perfect as a main meal with rice or as a side dish.
instructions: Clean the mushrooms thoroughly and cut large ones into halves or quarters.
Blend the tatashe, scotch bonnet, and onion until smooth.
Heat the vegetable oil and fry the blended pepper mixture for about 10–12 minutes until the raw taste disappears.
Season with seasoning cubes, thyme, curry, and salt to taste.
Add the mushrooms and toss gently until well coated with the pepper sauce.
Cook over medium-high heat for 8–10 minutes until the mushrooms are tender but still juicy.
Serve hot with white rice, fried rice, jollof rice, boiled yam, or as a side dish.
author: API Food Database

name: Nigerian Lentil Stew
description: A hearty and nutritious Nigerian-style lentil stew simmered in a rich tomato and pepper sauce with aromatic local spices. Packed with plant protein, fiber, and bold flavors, it's an affordable and satisfying meal for the whole family.
instructions: Rinse the lentils thoroughly under running water.
Blend the tomatoes, onions, and scotch bonnet until smooth.
Heat the vegetable oil in a pot and fry the blended mixture for about 10–12 minutes until the sauce thickens.
Season with seasoning cubes, thyme, curry, and salt to taste.
Add the rinsed lentils and enough water or stock to cover.
Cook for 20–25 minutes until the lentils are tender and the stew thickens.
Adjust seasoning if needed and serve hot with white rice, boiled yam, bread, or plantain.
author: API Food Database

name: Smoked Turkey Stew
description: A rich and smoky Nigerian stew made with smoked turkey pieces simmered in a flavorful tomato and pepper sauce. The natural smokiness of the turkey blends beautifully with aromatic spices to create a hearty stew perfect with rice, yam, plantain, or bread.
instructions: Cut the smoked turkey into serving-size pieces and rinse briefly.
Blend the tomatoes, tatashe, onions, and scotch bonnet until smooth.
Heat the vegetable oil in a pot and fry the blended mixture for 15–20 minutes until thick and the raw taste disappears.
Season with seasoning cubes, thyme, curry, and salt to taste.
Add the smoked turkey and stir gently until well coated.
Pour in a little stock or water if needed and simmer for 10–15 minutes so the turkey absorbs the sauce.
Adjust seasoning and serve hot with white rice, boiled yam, plantain, potatoes, or bread.
author: API Food Database

name: Plantain Pancakes
description: Fluffy and naturally sweet Nigerian plantain pancakes made with mashed ripe plantains, flour, eggs, and milk. Soft on the inside with lightly crisp edges, they make a delicious breakfast or brunch served with honey, syrup, or fresh fruit.
instructions: Peel and mash the ripe plantains until smooth.
Whisk the eggs and add the milk.
Mix in the mashed plantains and flour until a smooth batter forms.
Add a pinch of salt and a little cinnamon or nutmeg if desired.
Heat a lightly oiled frying pan over medium heat.
Pour about 1/4 cup of batter for each pancake and cook until bubbles appear.
Flip and cook the other side until golden brown.
Serve warm with honey, maple syrup, butter, or fresh fruit.
author: API Food Database

name: Nigerian Shakshuka
description: A Nigerian twist on the Middle Eastern classic—eggs poached directly in a rich and spicy tomato stew made with tatashe, scotch bonnet, and local seasonings. This hearty one-pan breakfast is perfect with Agege bread, toast, or flatbread.
instructions: Blend the tomatoes, tatashe, onion, and scotch bonnet until smooth.
Heat the vegetable oil in a wide frying pan and fry the blended mixture for 15–20 minutes until thick and well reduced.
Season with salt, seasoning cubes, curry, thyme, and black pepper to taste.
Use the back of a spoon to make 8 small wells in the sauce.
Crack one egg into each well.
Cover the pan and cook over low heat for 6–8 minutes until the egg whites are set while the yolks remain slightly runny, or cook longer if preferred.
Garnish with chopped spring onions or parsley if desired and serve immediately with toasted bread, Agege bread, pita, or flatbread.
author: API Food Database

name: Yam Fritters
description: Crispy and savory Nigerian yam fritters made from mashed yam mixed with eggs, onions, peppers, and spices before being pan-fried until golden brown. Crunchy on the outside, soft inside, and perfect as a snack, breakfast, or side dish.
instructions: Peel, wash, and boil the yam until soft, then drain and mash until smooth.
Beat the eggs and mix them into the mashed yam.
Add finely diced onion, chopped scotch bonnet, salt, seasoning, and a little black pepper.
Mix thoroughly until well combined.
Shape the mixture into flat patties using your hands or a spoon.
Heat vegetable oil in a frying pan over medium heat.
Fry the fritters for 3–4 minutes per side until golden brown and crispy.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot with pepper sauce, ketchup, or a fresh vegetable salad.
author: API Food Database

name: Akara Burger
description: A bold Nigerian fusion burger featuring a crispy akara bean fritter served in a toasted burger bun with fresh coleslaw, sliced tomatoes, and spicy pepper sauce. A delicious plant-based twist that combines classic Nigerian flavors with a modern burger experience.
instructions: Soak the beans for 30 minutes, peel the skins, and rinse thoroughly.
Blend the beans with onion, scotch bonnet, and a small amount of water until smooth and fluffy.
Season with salt and seasoning cubes, then whisk the batter for a few minutes to incorporate air.
Heat the vegetable oil and fry large spoonfuls of the batter into thick akara patties until golden brown on both sides.
Drain the akara on paper towels.
Lightly toast the burger buns.
Spread pepper sauce or mayonnaise on the buns if desired.
Layer coleslaw, the akara patty, sliced tomatoes, and additional onions before covering with the top bun.
Serve immediately with fries, plantain chips, or a chilled drink.
author: API Food Database

name: Nigerian Smoothie Bowl
description: A vibrant and nutritious smoothie bowl made from blended Nigerian tropical fruits—mango, pawpaw, and banana—topped with crunchy granola, fresh fruit slices, coconut flakes, and a drizzle of honey. A refreshing breakfast packed with vitamins and natural sweetness.
instructions: Peel and chop the mangoes, pawpaw, and bananas.
Add the fruits to a blender together with the milk or yogurt.
Blend until thick, creamy, and completely smooth.
Pour the smoothie evenly into two large serving bowls.
Top with granola, coconut flakes, and fresh fruit slices.
Drizzle honey over each bowl.
Serve immediately while chilled.
author: API Food Database

name: Ofada Rice with Coconut Stew
description: A premium Nigerian fusion dish pairing aromatic Ofada rice with a rich coconut-infused tomato stew and tender chicken. The creamy coconut milk balances the bold peppery flavors, creating a delicious twist on a beloved Nigerian classic.
instructions: Wash the Ofada rice thoroughly and cook until tender. Drain and set aside.
Season the chicken with salt, seasoning cubes, curry, thyme, and garlic, then boil until tender. Fry or grill lightly until golden.
Blend the tomatoes, tatashe, scotch bonnet, and one onion until smooth.
Heat the vegetable oil and fry the sliced remaining onion for 2 minutes.
Add the blended pepper mixture and fry for about 15–20 minutes until the sauce thickens.
Pour in the coconut milk and stir well.
Add the cooked chicken and some chicken stock. Simmer for another 10 minutes.
Adjust seasoning and cook until the stew becomes rich and creamy.
Serve the coconut stew generously over hot Ofada rice.
author: API Food Database

name: Honey Beans with Coconut
description: A creamy and naturally sweet Nigerian beans dish cooked in rich coconut milk with palm oil, crayfish, and aromatic spices. The coconut milk transforms ordinary beans into a luxurious and comforting one-pot meal.
instructions: Pick through the beans to remove stones and dirt, then rinse thoroughly.
Soak the beans for 2 hours or overnight to reduce cooking time (optional).
Transfer the beans to a pot and add enough water to cover them by about 3 inches.
Cook until the beans are almost tender, about 45 minutes, adding more water if needed.
Add the diced onions and scotch bonnet.
Pour in the coconut milk and stir gently.
Add the palm oil, crayfish, seasoning cubes, and salt.
Cook uncovered on medium-low heat for another 20 minutes until the beans are soft and the sauce becomes creamy.
Adjust seasoning to taste.
Serve hot as a complete meal or alongside fried plantain.
author: API Food Database

name: Nigerian Bean Burger
description: A creative and satisfying Nigerian plant-based burger made from spiced bean patties pan-fried until crispy, served in toasted buns with coleslaw, sliced tomatoes, and a bold pepper sauce. Filling, flavorful, and completely standalone.
instructions: Cook the beans until very soft if not already cooked. Drain completely and allow to cool.
Mash the beans thoroughly, leaving a little texture.
Finely dice the onion and scotch bonnet and mix into the beans.
Add the eggs, breadcrumbs, seasoning cubes, and a little salt. Mix until the mixture holds together.
Divide into 4 equal portions and shape into thick burger patties.
Refrigerate for 15 minutes to help the patties firm up.
Heat the vegetable oil over medium heat and fry each patty for 4–5 minutes per side until golden brown and crispy.
Toast the burger buns lightly.
Assemble each burger with coleslaw, bean patty, sliced tomatoes, and pepper sauce.
Serve immediately while hot.
author: API Food Database

name: Stuffed Agege Bread
description: A spectacular Nigerian breakfast of thick Agege bread hollowed out and filled with a spiced egg, sausage, and vegetable mixture, then baked or pan-fried until golden. A complete meal in a bread boat that is hearty, satisfying, and perfect for sharing.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C or heat a large frying pan over medium heat.
Slice the loaf into 4 thick pieces, about 4–5 cm each.
Using a small knife, carefully cut a deep pocket into each slice without cutting through the sides or bottom.
Scoop out some of the bread interior to create a cavity for the filling.
Dice the sausage, green pepper, tomatoes, and onion into small pieces.
Beat the eggs and mix with the vegetables, sausage, seasoning cubes, and salt.
Melt the butter in a pan and lightly scramble the egg mixture until just beginning to set.
Fill each bread pocket generously with the egg mixture.
Brush the outside of the bread with melted butter.
Bake for 12–15 minutes until the bread is toasted and the filling is fully set, or pan-fry for 3–4 minutes per side until golden brown.
Serve immediately while hot.
author: API Food Database

name: Nigerian Bread Pudding
description: A warm and indulgent Nigerian-style bread pudding made from cubed stale bread soaked in a spiced egg and coconut milk custard, then baked until golden and set. A creative and delicious way to transform leftover bread into a comforting dessert or breakfast.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 170°C and grease a medium baking dish with butter.
Cut the stale bread into 2 cm cubes and spread evenly in the baking dish.
Sprinkle the raisins over the bread if using.
In a large bowl, whisk together the eggs, coconut milk, sugar, cinnamon, nutmeg, and vanilla extract until smooth.
Pour the custard evenly over the bread cubes, ensuring every piece is soaked.
Press the bread down gently with a spoon and allow it to soak for 10 minutes.
Dot the surface with small pieces of butter.
Bake for 40–45 minutes until the top is golden brown and the custard is fully set.
Allow to cool for 5–10 minutes before slicing.
Serve warm on its own or with a drizzle of condensed milk or custard.
author: API Food Database

name: Bread and Omelette Stack
description: A satisfying Nigerian breakfast stack of toasted bread layered with a thick spiced omelette loaded with peppers, onions, and tomatoes. Simple to prepare yet impressive and completely filling as a standalone meal.
instructions: Dice the tomato, onion, green pepper, and scotch bonnet into small pieces.
Beat the eggs in a bowl, add the seasoning cube and a pinch of salt, then whisk well.
Heat the butter in a non-stick frying pan over medium heat.
Add the diced vegetables and sauté for about 2 minutes until slightly softened.
Pour the beaten eggs over the vegetables and cook without stirring until almost set.
Fold the omelette in half and cook for another minute.
Toast the bread slices in a little butter until golden on both sides.
Place one slice of toast on a plate, top with half of the omelette, and cover with another slice. Repeat for the second serving.
Serve immediately while hot.
author: API Food Database

name: Nigerian Garlic Bread with Sardine
description: A bold and satisfying Nigerian twist on garlic bread—thick slices of Agege bread spread with rich garlic butter, topped with a savory sardine and tomato mixture, then toasted until golden. Perfect as a hearty breakfast, snack, or light meal.
instructions: Preheat the oven or grill to 200°C.
Mince the garlic and mix it with softened butter and chopped parsley or scent leaves.
Slice the loaf into 8 thick slices or cut it in half lengthwise.
Spread the garlic butter generously over each slice.
Mix the drained sardines with diced tomatoes, onion, scotch bonnet, and the crushed seasoning cube.
Spoon the sardine mixture evenly over the bread.
Arrange on a baking tray and bake or grill for 8–10 minutes until the bread is crisp around the edges and the topping is hot.
Garnish with extra parsley or scent leaves if desired.
Serve immediately while warm.
author: API Food Database

name: Sardine Stuffed Bread Roll
description: Soft dinner rolls hollowed out and filled with a creamy spiced sardine, egg, and vegetable mixture, then baked until golden. A hearty portable meal that's perfect for breakfast, lunch, or a satisfying snack.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C.
Cut the tops off the bread rolls and set them aside as lids.
Carefully scoop out some of the soft bread inside each roll, leaving about a 1 cm wall.
Brush the inside of each roll lightly with melted butter.
Drain the sardines and flake them into a bowl.
Add the diced tomato, onion, scotch bonnet, chopped boiled eggs, mayonnaise, and crushed seasoning cube.
Mix gently until everything is well combined.
Fill each bread roll generously with the sardine mixture.
Replace the bread lids and brush the outside with melted butter.
Bake for 12–15 minutes until the rolls are lightly golden and the filling is heated through.
Serve warm as a complete breakfast, lunch, or snack.
author: API Food Database

name: Yam Pepper Soup
description: A warming and aromatic Nigerian pepper soup with tender yam chunks as the star ingredient, cooked in a deeply spiced broth with uziza leaves and crayfish. A comforting standalone meal that is light yet deeply satisfying.

ingredientsAlternatives.name: Pepper soup spice
alternatives: Uziza seed + uda seed + ehuru blend

instructions: Peel the yam and cut it into medium-sized chunks; rinse thoroughly.
Bring about 4 cups of water to a boil in a pot.
Add the diced onion, scotch bonnet, and crayfish.
Add the yam pieces and cook over medium heat.
Stir in the pepper soup spice and seasoning cubes.
Cook for 20–25 minutes until the yam is tender.
Taste and adjust the seasoning if needed.
Add the uziza leaves and simmer for another 3–4 minutes.
Serve hot with plenty of the flavorful broth.
author: API Food Database

name: Baked Yam with Coconut Sauce
description: Thick yam slices brushed with spiced oil and oven-baked until caramelized and tender, served with a rich creamy coconut dipping sauce. An elegant and modern way to enjoy yam that impresses with minimal effort.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C and lightly grease a baking tray.
Peel the yam and cut into thick wedges or rounds about 2 cm thick.
Mix the vegetable oil, mixed spice, garlic powder, salt, and crushed seasoning cube.
Coat the yam pieces evenly with the seasoned oil.
Arrange the yam in a single layer on the baking tray.
Bake for 20 minutes, then turn the pieces over.
Bake for another 20–25 minutes until golden brown and tender.
Meanwhile, heat the coconut milk in a saucepan over low heat.
Add the diced onion and scotch bonnet, then simmer for about 10 minutes.
Taste and adjust the seasoning if necessary.
Serve the baked yam hot with the warm coconut sauce on the side for dipping.
author: API Food Database

name: Stuffed Yam Balls
description: Crispy golden yam balls filled with a spiced minced beef and vegetable mixture, rolled in breadcrumbs and deep fried until perfectly crunchy outside. A show-stopping Nigerian snack or party appetizer that is completely self-contained.
instructions: Peel and boil the yam until very soft, then drain and mash until smooth.
Season the mashed yam lightly with salt and allow it to cool.
Heat a little oil and fry the minced beef with diced onion, scotch bonnet, mixed vegetables, and seasoning cubes until dry and well cooked.
Allow the beef filling to cool completely.
Divide the mashed yam into 12 equal portions.
Flatten each portion, place some beef filling in the center, and seal to form a smooth ball.
Beat the eggs in a bowl and place the breadcrumbs on a plate.
Dip each yam ball in egg, then coat evenly with breadcrumbs.
Heat the vegetable oil and fry the yam balls in batches until golden brown and crispy.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot with pepper sauce.
author: API Food Database

name: Yam and Coconut Porridge
description: A creamy and comforting Nigerian yam porridge slow cooked in coconut milk with palm oil, crayfish, and scent leaves. Rich, naturally sweet from the coconut, and deeply satisfying as a standalone meal.
instructions: Peel the yam and cut it into medium-sized cubes; rinse well.
Place the yam in a pot and add enough water to just cover it.
Add the diced onion, scotch bonnet, and palm oil, then bring to a boil.
Stir in the crayfish and seasoning cubes.
Cook over medium heat for about 15 minutes until the yam begins to soften.
Pour in the coconut milk and stir gently.
Continue cooking for another 15–20 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Mash a few pieces of yam with the back of a spoon to naturally thicken the porridge.
Add the scent leaves and cook for another 3 minutes.
Taste, adjust the salt if needed, and serve hot.
author: API Food Database

name: Yam and Corned Beef Hash
description: A hearty and flavorful Nigerian hash of diced fried yam tossed with spiced corned beef, onions, tomatoes, and peppers all pan fried together until golden and caramelized. A complete and satisfying breakfast or lunch.
instructions: Peel yam and dice into small 2cm cubes; rinse and pat dry with paper towels.
Heat oil in a large frying pan or wok over medium-high heat.
Add yam cubes; fry for 10-12 minutes stirring occasionally until golden and slightly crispy on all sides.
Remove fried yam and drain on paper towels; set aside.
In the same pan with residual oil, add diced onion; fry for 2 minutes.
Add diced tomato, scotch bonnet, and green pepper; stir fry for 3 minutes.
Add corned beef; break into pieces with a spoon and stir fry for 3 minutes.
Add seasoning cube and salt; mix well.
Return fried yam to the pan; toss everything together gently.
Press down lightly and allow to cook undisturbed for 2 minutes to develop a slight crust.
Stir and cook for another 3 minutes until everything is well combined and slightly caramelized.
Serve hot directly from the pan as a complete meal.
author: API Food Database

name: Nigerian Chicken Wings
description: Crispy and boldly spiced Nigerian chicken wings marinated in a suya and pepper blend then fried until perfectly golden. Tossed in a spicy pepper glaze for an extra layer of flavor — the ultimate Nigerian party snack that stands completely alone.
instructions: Clean chicken wings and pat completely dry with paper towels — this ensures crispiness.
Make small cuts into the thickest parts of the wings to allow marinade to penetrate.
Blend garlic and ginger to a paste; combine with suya spice, seasoning, and salt.
Coat chicken wings thoroughly in the spice marinade; cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour.
Heat oil in a deep pot to 175°C.
Fry chicken wings in batches — do not overcrowd the pot.
Fry each batch for 12–15 minutes until deep golden brown and cooked through.
While wings fry, blend tatashe and scotch bonnet; fry in 2 tbsp oil for 10 minutes as a glaze.
Drain fried wings on paper towels to remove excess oil.
Toss hot wings in the pepper glaze; coat evenly.
Arrange on a serving platter and serve immediately while hot and crispy.
These wings are a complete meal on their own.
author: API Food Database

name: Spiced Boiled Corn with Coconut Milk
description: Fresh corn on the cob slow cooked in a fragrant broth of coconut milk, spices, and scotch bonnet until deeply infused with flavor. A creamy, aromatic, and completely satisfying Nigerian street food upgrade.
instructions: Remove husks and silk from corn cobs; rinse under cold water.
Cut each corn cob in half or leave whole depending on preference.
Place corn in a large pot; add enough water to almost cover.
Pour in coconut milk; add sliced onion and scotch bonnet.
Add mixed spice and salt; stir the liquid gently.
Bring to a boil over high heat; reduce to medium and cover pot.
Cook for 30-35 minutes turning corn occasionally to ensure even cooking.
The corn should be tender and the liquid will have reduced and become creamy.
Remove corn from pot; brush generously with butter on all sides.
Serve hot — the coconut milk broth that remains can also be sipped as a drink.
Each corn cob is a complete satisfying snack or light meal on its own.
author: API Food Database

name: Nigerian Loaded Yam Fries
description: Crispy golden yam fries piled high and loaded with spiced pepper stew, shredded chicken, diced tomatoes, and a drizzle of creamy garlic sauce. A bold and indulgent Nigerian fusion dish that is a complete meal in a bowl.
instructions: Peel yam and cut into thick fry shapes about 1cm wide; rinse and pat completely dry.
Season with salt and a pinch of mixed spice.
Heat oil to 180°C; fry yam fries in batches for 8-10 minutes until golden and crispy.
Drain on paper towels; sprinkle with salt immediately.
Season chicken with seasoning and salt; grill or pan fry until cooked through.
Shred chicken into strips; set aside.
Blend tatashe and scotch bonnet; fry in 2 tbsp oil for 10 minutes as pepper sauce.
Mince garlic finely; mix with mayonnaise and a pinch of salt for garlic sauce.
Pile yam fries generously on a large plate or in a bowl.
Spoon pepper stew over the fries.
Top with shredded chicken and diced fresh tomato.
Drizzle garlic mayo generously over the top.
Serve immediately while fries are still crispy.
author: API Food Database

name: Plantain Lasagna
description: A spectacular Nigerian fusion baked dish with layers of fried ripe plantain, well seasoned minced beef sauce, and a creamy bechamel all baked together until golden and bubbling. A show-stopping complete meal that will wow any guest.

ingredientsAlternatives.name: Ripe plantain
alternatives: Unripe plantain for less sweet version

instructions: Peel plantain and slice diagonally into 1cm thick slices.
Fry plantain slices in hot oil until golden on both sides; drain and set aside.
Fry minced beef with diced onion until browned; add blended tomatoes and seasoning.
Cook meat sauce for 15 minutes until thick and well seasoned.
Make bechamel: melt butter in a saucepan; whisk in flour for 1 minute.
Gradually pour in milk while whisking constantly to avoid lumps.
Cook on medium heat for 5 minutes, stirring until thick and smooth; season with salt.
Preheat oven to 180°C; grease a baking dish.
Layer 1: spread a thin layer of meat sauce on the bottom of the dish.
Layer 2: arrange fried plantain slices to cover the sauce completely.
Layer 3: spoon more meat sauce over the plantain.
Layer 4: another layer of plantain slices.
Layer 5: pour bechamel sauce evenly over the top.
Sprinkle grated cheese generously over the bechamel.
Bake for 25-30 minutes until top is golden and bubbling.
Allow to rest for 10 minutes before slicing and serving.

name: Nigerian Loaded Yam Fries
description: Crispy golden yam fries piled high and loaded with spiced pepper stew, shredded chicken, diced tomatoes, and a drizzle of creamy garlic sauce. A bold and indulgent Nigerian fusion dish that is a complete meal in a bowl.
instructions: Peel yam and cut into thick fry shapes about 1cm wide; rinse and pat completely dry.
Season with salt and a pinch of mixed spice.
Heat oil to 180°C; fry yam fries in batches for 8-10 minutes until golden and crispy.
Drain on paper towels; sprinkle with salt immediately.
Season chicken with seasoning and salt; grill or pan fry until cooked through.
Shred chicken into strips; set aside.
Blend tatashe and scotch bonnet; fry in 2 tbsp oil for 10 minutes as pepper sauce.
Mince garlic finely; mix with mayonnaise and a pinch of salt for garlic sauce.
Pile yam fries generously on a large plate or in a bowl.
Spoon pepper stew over the fries.
Top with shredded chicken and diced fresh tomato.
Drizzle garlic mayo generously over the top.
Serve immediately while fries are still crispy.

name: Nigerian Deviled Eggs
description: Classic deviled eggs given a bold Nigerian twist — the yolk filling is spiced with scotch bonnet, suya spice, and crayfish for an unforgettable punch of flavor. An elegant party appetizer that is completely standalone.
instructions: Place eggs in a single layer in a pot; cover with cold water by 2cm.
Bring to a boil; once boiling cover the pot and remove from heat.
Let eggs sit in hot water for exactly 12 minutes for perfect hard-boiled yolks.
Transfer to a bowl of ice-cold water immediately; allow to cool for 10 minutes.
Peel eggs carefully under running water and pat dry.
Slice each egg in half lengthwise using a sharp knife.
Remove the yolks and place them in a bowl; arrange the egg white halves on a serving plate.
Mash the yolks with a fork until completely smooth.
Add mayonnaise, finely minced scotch bonnet, crayfish, and suya spice.
Mix until creamy and well combined; season with salt to taste.
Transfer the filling into a piping bag or use a spoon to fill each egg white half.
Garnish with paprika and sliced spring onions.
Refrigerate for 15 minutes before serving. Serve chilled.

name: Spiced Roasted Groundnuts
description: Boldly seasoned Nigerian roasted groundnuts coated in a spiced mixture of suya spice, garlic, and salt then oven-roasted until perfectly crunchy. A highly addictive Nigerian snack that is protein-rich and completely satisfying on its own.
instructions: Preheat oven to 160°C; line a baking tray with parchment paper.
Pick through groundnuts to remove any bad ones; place in a bowl.
Add vegetable oil to the groundnuts and toss to coat lightly.
In a small bowl, mix suya spice, garlic powder, cayenne pepper, and salt.
Pour the spice mixture over the oiled groundnuts and toss thoroughly until evenly coated.
Spread the groundnuts in a single layer on the prepared baking tray without overlapping.
Roast in the preheated oven for 20–25 minutes, stirring halfway through.
Watch carefully during the last 5 minutes to prevent burning.
Roast until golden brown and fragrant; the groundnuts will become crispier as they cool.
Remove from the oven and spread on a tray or plate to cool completely.
Store in an airtight container after cooling.
Serve as a crunchy snack.

name: Bean and Vegetable Medley
description: A colorful and nutritious Nigerian one-pot dish of creamy brown beans cooked together with diced carrots, green beans, spinach, and palm oil. Protein-rich, fiber-packed, and deeply flavorful — a wholesome standalone meal.
instructions: Soak beans for 2 hours or overnight; drain and rinse well.
Cook beans in fresh water over medium heat for 30 minutes until almost tender.
Dice carrot into small cubes; trim and cut green beans into 2cm pieces.
Add palm oil to the beans; stir to combine.
Add diced onion, scotch bonnet, crayfish, and seasoning cubes.
Add diced carrot; cook for 10 minutes until carrot begins to soften.
Add green beans; cook for another 8 minutes.
Add spinach last; stir gently and cook for 3 more minutes.
The beans should be soft and creamy with the vegetables tender but not mushy.
Taste and adjust seasoning if needed.
Serve hot in bowls as a complete meal.

name: Yam and Vegetable Stir Fry
description: A vibrant and satisfying Nigerian stir fry of diced yam cooked until golden then tossed with colorful vegetables, eggs, and soy sauce. Quick, healthy, and packed with flavor — a complete one-pan meal ready in 30 minutes.
instructions: Peel yam and dice into small 2cm cubes; rinse and pat completely dry.
Heat 2 tbsp oil in a wok or large frying pan over high heat.
Add yam cubes; stir fry for 10–12 minutes, tossing frequently until golden and slightly crispy.
Remove yam and set aside; keep pan on heat.
Add remaining oil; add diced onion and scotch bonnet and stir fry for 2 minutes.
Add mixed vegetables; stir fry on high heat for 3–4 minutes until tender-crisp.
Push vegetables to the side; crack eggs into the center of the pan.
Scramble eggs quickly until just set, then mix with the vegetables.
Return fried yam to the pan; pour soy sauce over everything.
Add seasoning cube and toss all ingredients together on high heat for 2–3 minutes.
Taste and adjust salt if needed.
Serve immediately while hot as a complete one-pan meal.

name: Crispy Yam Waffles
description: A creative and impressive Nigerian breakfast of grated yam mixed with eggs and spices then cooked in a waffle iron until crispy and golden. Served with a spiced egg topping for a complete and stunning meal.
instructions: Peel yam and grate coarsely using a box grater; squeeze out as much moisture as possible using a clean cloth.
Place grated yam in a bowl; add 2 beaten eggs, flour, seasoning, and salt.
Finely dice half the onion and scotch bonnet; add to yam mixture.
Mix until well combined — the batter should hold together when pressed.
Preheat waffle iron and brush generously with melted butter.
Spoon yam mixture into waffle iron; close and cook for 5–7 minutes until crispy and golden.
While waffles cook, prepare topping: dice tomato and remaining onion.
Scramble remaining 2 eggs with tomato, onion, and seasoning in a pan with butter.
Cook until eggs are fluffy and slightly wet — not overdone.
Remove yam waffles carefully from waffle iron.
Top each waffle generously with spiced scrambled egg mixture.
Serve immediately while waffles are still crispy.

name: Nigerian Bruschetta
description: A stylish Nigerian twist on Italian bruschetta — toasted bread rubbed with garlic and topped with a bold mixture of diced tomatoes, avocado, crayfish, scotch bonnet, and scent leaves. Fresh, vibrant, and completely satisfying.
instructions: Slice bread into 1.5cm thick rounds or diagonal slices.
Brush both sides with oil; toast in a griddle pan or oven until golden and crispy on both sides.
While still hot, rub one side of each toast with a cut garlic clove — the heat releases the garlic oil.
Dice avocado into small cubes; dice tomatoes removing excess seeds and liquid.
Finely mince scotch bonnet and scent leaves.
Combine avocado, tomatoes, scotch bonnet, scent leaves, and crayfish in a bowl.
Drizzle with a little oil; add salt to taste and toss gently.
Taste the topping and adjust seasoning — it should be bold and fresh.
Spoon the topping generously onto each garlic-rubbed toast.
Serve immediately — the contrast of hot crunchy bread with fresh cold topping is key.
Arrange on a platter for a stunning presentation.

name: Coconut Beans Porridge
description: A luxurious and fragrant Nigerian beans porridge made creamy with coconut milk, sweetened naturally by honey beans, and enriched with palm oil and crayfish. Thick, comforting, and deeply satisfying as a standalone meal.
instructions: Pick through beans; soak overnight or for minimum 2 hours.
Drain and rinse soaked beans; transfer to a pot with fresh water.
Add diced onion and scotch bonnet; bring to a boil over high heat.
Reduce to medium heat; cook beans for 40-45 minutes until very soft.
The beans should be soft enough to mash easily between fingers.
Pour in coconut milk and palm oil; stir to combine.
Add crayfish and seasoning cubes; stir well.
Using the back of a wooden spoon mash some beans against the pot wall to thicken the porridge.
Cook on medium-low heat for another 20 minutes stirring every 5 minutes.
The porridge should be thick, creamy, and rich — not watery.
Add scent leaves; stir gently and cook for 3 more minutes.
Taste and adjust salt and seasoning.
Serve hot in deep bowls — this is a complete and satisfying meal.

name: Yam and Smoked Fish Pottage
description: A deeply flavorful Nigerian yam pottage elevated with rich smoked fish, ugwu leaves, palm oil, and crayfish. The smoky fish infuses the yam with an irresistible depth of flavor — a complete and nourishing one-pot meal.
instructions: Soak smoked fish in hot water for 5 minutes to soften; drain and debone carefully.
Flake fish into medium pieces; set aside.
Peel yam and cut into medium chunks about 5cm; rinse under cold water.
Place yam in a pot with just enough water to cover.
Add diced onion, scotch bonnet, palm oil, and crayfish.
Add seasoning cubes and a pinch of salt; bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to medium; cook for 15 minutes until yam begins to soften.
Add flaked smoked fish; stir gently into the pottage.
Continue cooking for 10-15 more minutes until yam is completely tender.
Using a wooden spoon, gently mash some yam pieces to thicken the pottage.
Add ugwu leaves; fold gently into the pottage.
Cook for 3-4 more minutes until leaves are wilted but still vibrant green.
Taste and adjust seasoning; serve hot in deep bowls.

name: Nigerian Egg Fried Plantain Bowl
description: A bold and satisfying Nigerian bowl of golden fried ripe plantain topped with fluffy scrambled eggs, spiced tomato sauce, and diced avocado. Beautiful to look at, quick to make, and completely standalone.
instructions: Peel plantain and slice diagonally into 1cm thick pieces.
Heat oil in a frying pan over medium heat until hot.
Fry plantain slices for 3-4 minutes each side until deep golden and caramelized.
Remove and drain on paper towels; arrange in a bowl as the base layer.
In the same pan with residual oil, fry diced onion for 2 minutes.
Add diced tomato and scotch bonnet; cook for 5 minutes until slightly thickened.
Season with seasoning cube and salt; set tomato sauce aside.
Beat eggs with a pinch of salt; scramble in a separate pan with a little oil.
Cook eggs slowly on low heat until fluffy and just set — do not overcook.
Dice avocado into cubes.
Assemble the bowl: plantain at the base, spiced tomato sauce spooned on one side, scrambled eggs on the other.
Top with fresh diced avocado.
Serve immediately while still warm.

name: Spiced Peanut Butter Toast
description: A bold and creative Nigerian toast topped with spiced groundnut paste, sliced banana, crayfish, and a drizzle of honey. The combination of savory and sweet flavors with Nigerian spice is surprisingly addictive and completely satisfying.

ingredients.name: Agege bread or whole wheat bread

instructions: Mix groundnut paste with suya spice, a pinch of crayfish, minced scotch bonnet, and salt in a small bowl.
Stir until all spices are evenly incorporated into the peanut butter.
Toast bread slices in a toaster or under the grill until golden and crispy.
Spread spiced groundnut paste generously and evenly on each slice of toast.
Slice banana into thin rounds; arrange overlapping slices on top of the peanut butter.
Drizzle honey over the banana slices.
Sprinkle a tiny pinch of suya spice over the top for garnish.
For an extra kick, add a few more drops of hot sauce or scotch bonnet.
Serve immediately while toast is still warm and crispy.
This toast is a complete energizing meal on its own.

name: Nigerian French Onion Bread
description: A bold Nigerian-inspired pull-apart bread loaded with deeply caramelized onions, suya-spiced butter, and melted cheese between each layer. Incredibly indulgent and completely satisfying as a standalone snack or light meal.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C.
Slice onions thinly; heat 2 tbsp butter in a pan over low heat.
Add onions and a pinch of salt; cook slowly for 20-25 minutes stirring occasionally.
Onions should turn deep golden brown and sweet — this caramelization is essential.
Add minced garlic and scotch bonnet; cook for 2 more minutes.
Mix remaining butter with suya spice until well combined.
Make diagonal cuts through the bread every 3cm without cutting all the way through the bottom.
Spread suya butter generously between each cut.
Spoon caramelized onions between each cut pressing gently.
Tuck grated cheese between each cut on top of the onions.
Wrap the whole loaf in foil; bake for 15 minutes.
Unwrap foil for the last 5 minutes to crisp and brown the top.
Serve immediately — pull apart to eat.

name: Bean and Plantain Skewers
description: A creative and fun Nigerian appetizer of spiced bean balls and golden fried plantain pieces alternated on skewers and served with a bold pepper dipping sauce. Visually stunning, delicious, and completely standalone.

ingredientsAlternatives.name: Ripe plantain
alternatives: Unripe plantain for less sweet version

instructions: Mash cooked beans thoroughly; add diced onion, one scotch bonnet, seasoning, and salt.
Mix in beaten egg and breadcrumbs until the mixture holds shape.
Roll into small balls about the size of a golf ball.
Peel plantain and cut into 3cm thick rounds.
Heat oil in a deep pan; fry plantain rounds for 3 minutes each side until golden.
In same oil fry bean balls for 4-5 minutes until golden and crispy all around.
Drain both on paper towels.
For dipping sauce: blend tatashe and remaining scotch bonnet; fry in 2 tbsp oil for 10 minutes.
Thread onto skewers alternating: plantain, bean ball, plantain, bean ball.
Arrange skewers on a platter.
Serve immediately with spicy dipping sauce on the side.

name: Yam and Avocado Bowl
description: A beautiful and nutritious Nigerian bowl featuring golden baked yam wedges served over a creamy avocado mash with a spiced tomato salsa and crayfish drizzle. A modern, health-conscious, and completely satisfying standalone meal.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C; line a baking tray with foil.
Peel yam and cut into thick wedges; toss with oil, salt, and a pinch of mixed spice.
Arrange yam wedges on baking tray; bake for 20-25 minutes flipping once until golden and tender.
While yam bakes prepare avocado mash: scoop avocado flesh into a bowl.
Mash with a fork until creamy; add lime juice, salt, and a tiny pinch of scotch bonnet.
For spiced tomato salsa: finely dice tomato, onion, and scotch bonnet.
Mix together with a squeeze of lime juice and salt; stir in crayfish.
Let salsa sit for 5 minutes for flavors to develop.
Assemble bowls: spread avocado mash generously as the base.
Arrange hot baked yam wedges on top of the avocado.
Spoon spiced tomato and crayfish salsa over the yam.
Serve immediately — the contrast of warm yam with cool avocado is the magic.
